title: Back-end factory automation and standardisation: SATAS, GEM300/E142/RITdb adoption at OSATs, and AMHS in packaging plants
why_it_matters: Back-end assembly/test is far less automated than front-end fabs; SATAS (Intel, Daifuku, Murata, 38 members) targets standardised automated lines by 2028 and AMHS makers now sell into advanced packaging.
questions: How automated are OSAT and in-house back-end plants today and what blocks full automation?
Which SEMI standards (GEM300, E142, RITdb, A4 TEMS) are adopted at OSATs?
What has SATAS produced and who are its members and funders?
How large is AMHS demand from advanced packaging?

title: China fab-software localisation: domestic CIM/MES/EAP vendors, adoption at Chinese fabs and the 'validation deadlock'
why_it_matters: Frost & Sullivan puts foreign vendors (Applied, Siemens) at roughly half of China's RMB1.6bn semiconductor IMSS market in 2024, with domestic vendors forecast to grow 31% a year; this is a live localisation front not covered by tool or EDA units.
questions: Who are the main Chinese fab-software vendors (Glorysoft, the 2017-founded 'Company B', others) and which fabs use them?
How fast are SMIC, Hua Hong, CXMT and YMTC replacing foreign MES/CIM?
Do US export controls or Chinese data-security rules affect fab-software choices?
primary_sources: SSE STAR prospectuses of Chinese industrial-software firms
